title: Decode persisted inventory safely
scenario: The fulfillment service reads item 1's inventory row before deciding whether the customer's order for 3 can proceed. Schema checks help, but old or damaged data can still be malformed; reject it at the persistence boundary before policy treats it as valid stock.
instructions: Implement InventoryRow conversion in src/infrastructure/inventory_row.rs. Keep InventoryRow private with signed i64 columns. Derive SQLx FromRow, then implement TryFrom<InventoryRow> for InventoryObservation. Require a positive ItemId and available value that fits u32; reject negative or oversized availability. Map row decoding and conversion failures to InvalidStoredData. Use supplied migration and in-memory SQLite tests; do not change schema or tests.

hints.body: Keep SQLx's signed, runtime-decoded columns in a private InventoryRow. The domain value should contain validated ItemId and u32 availability.
Derive FromRow, convert item_id with ItemId::new, and convert available with u32::try_from. Any decode or conversion error becomes InvalidStoredData.
Implement TryFrom<InventoryRow> for InventoryObservation, then decode SqliteRow through InventoryRow::from_row and call try_into.

completionExplanation: Malformed inventory data now stops at the row adapter; valid rows become domain observations for the same fulfillment flow. Next, decrement stock and insert the reservation together so neither write can commit alone.
